b: I drew this week’s cartoon thinking of the age-old balancing act of advertising: how to make ads both engaging and brand-building.
The most effective ads are a mix of showmanship and salesmanship. They have to tell an entertaining story and be distinctive enough to be credited back to the brand. These goals are often in tension.

I once said “the best marketing doesn’t feel like marketing” at a conference and that quote went more viral than most of the cartoons I’ve drawn. And yet to be effective, marketing ultimately has to accomplish the business objectives we set for it.
“When I write an advertisement, I don’t want you to tell me that you find it ‘creative.’ I want you to find it so interesting that you buy the product.”

The way marketers typically brief agencies doesn’t help. Briefs are often written by committee, and frequently include a gauntlet of “creative mandatories” that can hobble ideas before they have a chance.
A 2021 BetterBriefs study by Matt Davies and Pieter-Paul von Weiler found that 80% of marketers believe they write good briefs. Only 10% of agencies agree.

The same balancing act is showing up in how brands work with creators. Kantar recently found that only 6% of creator content delivers both strong platform engagement and strong brand-building potential.
And yet, as ​Ligia Patrocinio, global marketing director at Heineken, put it:

“Brands aren’t simply buying reach when they work with creators … the moment you treat a creator like an ad placement, you lose the very thing that makes the creator content a true success with audiences: authenticity, cultural fit and personality.”
Somewhere along the way, “doesn’t feel like marketing” became one more mandatory.
